answer: Forced-path task routing. Each identity must periodically solve a randomly assigned navigation task through a shared synthetic environment (procedural terrain, e.g. crossing a tundra basin) and report a verifiable route trace. Enforcement: duplicate identities controlled by one operator tend to produce correlated traces—similar wander patterns or identical inlet choices—because the operator reuses routing logic or cached solutions. Independent agents diverge. The verifier flags trace clusters and quarantines them.
